theme: Peter freed; the first missionary journey begins
readingInstruction: Read Acts 12:1-13:52. James is killed, Peter is freed from prison, Herod dies, and the Holy Spirit sends out Barnabas and Saul on the first missionary journey. Paul preaches in Pisidian Antioch. Notice the role of prayer and the Spirit in every stage.
settingTheScene: Persecution intensifies under King Herod Agrippa I. He kills James the brother of John and arrests Peter. Then the scene moves to Antioch, where the church worships and fasts. What follows is a new stage in Acts: the church deliberately sends missionaries to the Gentile world. From here on, the focus shifts from Peter to Paul, and the geography widens.
observation: “So Peter was kept in prison, but earnest prayer for him was made to God by the church” (12:5).
“And the angel struck Peter on the side and woke him, saying, Get up quickly” (12:7).
“But the word of God increased and multiplied” (12:24).
“While they were worshiping the Lord and fasting, the Holy Spirit said, Set apart for me Barnabas and Saul for the work to which I have called them” (13:2).
“And by him everyone who believes is freed from everything from which you could not be freed by the law of Moses” (13:39).
“For so the Lord has commanded us, saying, I have made you a light for the Gentiles, that you may bring salvation to the ends of the earth” (13:47).
“And when the Gentiles heard this, they began rejoicing and glorifying the word of the Lord, and as many as were appointed to eternal life believed” (13:48).
“And the disciples were filled with joy and with the Holy Spirit” (13:52).
interpretation:
James is executed with the sword, and Herod, seeing that it pleases the Jews, arrests Peter. He plans to bring him out after Passover. “So Peter was kept in prison, but earnest prayer for him was made to God by the church.” The night before the trial, Peter is sleeping between two soldiers, chained. An angel wakes him, the chains fall off, and the iron gate opens by itself. Peter thinks it is a vision until he is in the street. At the house of Mary, the mother of John Mark, the church is praying, and when Rhoda announces that Peter is at the door, they say, “You are out of your mind!” Their prayers were answered, and they could hardly believe it. Herod later gives a speech, the crowd cries, “The voice of a god, and not of a man!” and an angel strikes him down because he did not give God the glory. “But the word of God increased and multiplied.” Kings fall, and the word advances.

In Antioch, the church has prophets and teachers, including Barnabas and Saul. While they are worshiping and fasting, the Holy Spirit says, “Set apart for me Barnabas and Saul for the work to which I have called them.” After fasting and prayer, they lay hands on them and send them. They sail to Cyprus, where Saul, who is now called Paul, confronts a magician and the proconsul Sergius Paulus believes. Then they go to Pisidian Antioch, where Paul preaches in the synagogue. His sermon moves from Israel’s history to David and then to Jesus, the Savior raised from the dead. “Let it be known to you therefore, brothers, that through this man forgiveness of sins is proclaimed to you, and by him everyone who believes is freed from everything from which you could not be freed by the law of Moses.” This is justification by faith in Christ.

The next Sabbath, almost the whole city gathers. The Jews are jealous and contradict Paul. Paul and Barnabas say boldly, “It was necessary that the word of God be spoken first to you. Since you thrust it aside, behold, we are turning to the Gentiles.” They cite Isaiah 49:6, “I have made you a light for the Gentiles.” The Gentiles rejoice, and “as many as were appointed to eternal life believed.” God’s sovereign choice and the human response are held together. The word spreads throughout the region. The Jews stir up persecution and drive them out, but the disciples are “filled with joy and with the Holy Spirit.”
connection: Isaiah 49:6 is the commission quoted in 13:47. Psalm 2:7, Isaiah 55:3, and Psalm 16:10 are quoted in Paul’s sermon in 13:33-35. Romans 3:21-28 and Galatians 2:16 develop justification by faith. Genesis 12:3 shows the Abrahamic promise at work. Romans 9 to 11 discusses God’s election and Israel. Ephesians 1:4-5 speaks of being chosen. 2 Corinthians 12:10 says that when I am weak, then I am strong. Psalm 34:7 says the angel of the LORD encamps around those who fear him.
application:
Pray earnestly for someone in danger or need, and expect God to answer, even if your faith is small.

Ask what the Spirit might be setting you apart for. Fast and pray with your church.

Remember that forgiveness is received by faith, not by law.
prayerPrompts: Thank God for answering the church’s prayers.
Ask him to set apart workers for his harvest.
Ask him to make you willing to go or to send.
